paragraphs: A document-grounded RAG chatbot with real user accounts. Sign up, upload your own documents (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, or plain text), then ask questions — DocuBot answers strictly from your documents, cites which one it pulled from, and keeps per-user conversation history that survives a restart.

similarity is the cosine similarity between the question embedding and the chunk embedding, in [0, 1]. It is a relative closeness signal, not a probability or a percent-confidence. The UI displays it as similarity 0.62, not 62%. Retrieval ranks by a combined score (relevance) that also weights lexical term overlap; DOCUBOTMINRELEVANCE is the confident floor. Below it DocuBot still tries the closest chunks and lets the grounded model decide whether they answer the question, so a paraphrase or a meta question ("summarize this") is not silently dropped by the threshold.
features: 🔐 Real accounts — email + password signup/login with Argon2id hashing, opaque HttpOnly session
👤 Per-user isolation — each account sees only its own documents and conversations; every read/write is
ownership-checked server-side (never trusted from the client)
💬 Multiple conversations — a sidebar of recent chats you can open, rename, and delete; history is stored
